claims.text: q5 (proposed): the worker reads the mesh collector's cached liveness observation with a freshness bound of 5 minutes and refuses to lease only when the observation is fresh AND session_ok=false AND a fallback_actor is registered; a stale or missing observation leases as today. obligations.behavior: a closed-unmerged PR emits one pr.closed fact and never pr.merged; its parked runs are cancelled with reason pr_closed and its refs are declined
obligations.source_text: cleanup also runs when a PR is CLOSED without merge: the human-inbox tracker already observes github_pr_closed (mapping.py:53, tracker README required field 'reference') but no pr.closed fact or consumer exists in examples/ or internal/; on close the item's parked runs are cancelled with reason pr_closed and its refs are reported (unreachable from main, so never deleted) in the cleanup record

obligations.behavior: the land node's client has no merge endpoint and the two token scopes are documented
obligations.source_text: the culture-land account's tokens can push and reply but the land node never merges a PR: a fine-grained token with contents:write plus pull-requests:write is technically able to call the merge API, so the boundary is enforced by the node (no merge call) and audited by the honesty condition, keeping the lane doc's 'a person is always in it' property (pr-upkeep-lane.md:32-46) and human-merges-pr as the only merge path

obligations.behavior: two refs on one branch land in sequence with the second waiting on the lease; a stale rebase re-fetches once then routes
obligations.source_text: one land at a time per target branch: two land nodes for two runs on the same PR branch would race (the second rebase goes stale when the first pushes, and its push is non-fast-forward — the exact failure that produced the review-fix side branches); the land node takes a lease keyed by target branch, and a stale rebase re-fetches and rebases again before pushing, bounded to two rounds before routing to a human

obligations.seam: land node step records + idempotent re-run
obligations.behavior: one record per step reached; a re-run after push adds no second commit and posts no second reply
obligations.source_text: every land attempt is a stepwise record: the land node writes one record per step reached (fetch, rebase, gate, push, reply, resolve) with outcome, so a partial landing (pushed but not replied, replied but not resolved) is visible in the ledger and the node is idempotent on re-run — it detects a commit already on the branch, a reply already posted and a thread already resolved and skips them rather than pushing or replying twice

obligations.seam: runner boundary for land and cleanup
obligations.behavior: neither node runs in the control-plane process; both are fetched-by-digest code nodes under an engine account
obligations.source_text: land and cleanup nodes execute only through the headspace-cli runner boundary (PRD: never a shell, script or Docker socket in the control-plane process); they use the engine account's own credentials (bridge-push.env for git, the jira bridge for Jira, devex for PR replies) and never the operator's Access cookie (#314's principle) — a dial-in bearer for an AGENT actor is admitted to exactly three write routes today (agentMayWrite, internal/api/actorbearer.go:76-85) so any new record these nodes write lands via the runner's observed path or needs that write set widened

obligations.behavior: sweep.py's only control-plane write is POST /v1alpha1/events, it has no Jira write, and pr-upkeep.pr carries no subject
obligations.source_text: the sweep stays the sole event emitter with no control-plane write path beyond POST /v1alpha1/events and no Jira write path; pr-upkeep.pr keeps no subject (#268); vendored skill bodies are not edited and the assign-to-workforce worktree/branch conventions are overridden per CLAUDE.md

obligations.seam: examples/pr-upkeep readiness code node + human-merges-pr context_refs
obligations.behavior: the merge approval's context resolves to a collector output carrying ci, sonar, threads, devague-proposed and failing-evidence fields, and the approval is reachable only after the collector completed
obligations.source_text: merge-gate readiness (#317, gate half): the human-merges-pr approval binds a deterministic collector node's output (CI checks, SonarCloud count, unresolved threads, proposed devague records, failing evidence) through context_refs so the human surface resolves it — presentation metadata is lifted out of the executable spec by the compiler (compile_test.go:174-206) and never reaches a human task payload (humantask.go:106-142 carries pointers, not values), so 'the approval presents readiness' means a collector node plus a binding, not a presentation field; the collector reuses .claude/skills/cicd/scripts/pr-status.sh (Sonar gate, issues, hotspots, unresolved tally) and devex pr read for checks
